page_title: The Best Programmers I Know | Matthias Endler

summary.title: The Best Programmers I Know
summary.one_liner: Matthias Endler lists the habits he observed in exceptional developers, such as reading the reference, understanding tools deeply, reading error messages, writing well, and never guessing.
takeaways: Read the official reference or spec for a tool before relying on Stack Overflow or guesses.
Understand tools deeply: their history, present maintainers, limitations, and ecosystem.
Read error messages carefully; they often contain the answer.
Break hard problems into smaller pieces, and resist guessing when things are ambiguous.
Stay curious, keep learning, write and share knowledge, and keep solutions simple.
summary.summary: This is a personal essay in which the author describes traits he saw in the most exceptional developers he has worked with. Each short section names one trait, such as reading the reference, knowing tools well, reading error messages, breaking down problems, writing clearly, continuing to learn, and keeping code simple. The author supports points with examples from his own career, including job interviews, and occasionally cites PEP 20 and Einstein. The piece is opinion and advice rather than a tutorial, and it ends by saying the list is not a checklist.
